title: A 99% reserve factor taxes away supplier yield as a soft way to empty a frozen market
content:
The reserve factor is "the percentage of interest payments paid to the protocol," and it enters the supply rate directly: supply rate = utilization × borrow rate × (1 − reserve factor). Most SparkLend markets sit between 1% and 30%. tBTC (A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.2.1.13) records **99%**.

The rest of tBTC's configuration explains the setting. Reserve State is `Frozen`, so no new supply or borrowing is possible; LTV is 0% while the liquidation threshold remains at 70%, the deprecation signature; and `Borrowing: Yes` keeps existing debt serviceable. At 99%, the surviving suppliers collect one hundredth of the interest their capital earns.

The effect is to make staying costly without forcing anyone out. A frozen market can otherwise sit indefinitely: suppliers have no deadline, and the protocol cannot expel them without expropriation. Removing nearly all the yield converts an open-ended wind-down into one with a strong voluntary gradient, and the capital leaves on its own.

The reading is inferential — the Artifact states the parameter and not the intention — but the alternative readings are weak. A 99% reserve factor cannot be a revenue strategy in a market closed to new deposits, and it is not a risk control in any direct sense. Alongside the other frozen assets it is best understood as the third lever in SparkLend's deprecation toolkit: freeze the entrances, zero the borrowing power, and tax the yield until the remaining balance leaves.
description: tBTC is Frozen with borrowing still enabled and the protocol taking 99% of interest, so remaining suppliers earn almost nothing and have every reason to withdraw voluntarily.
